children.translated_text: by a jackal or a wolf,
upon the rising of a planet or <s>nakṣatra</s> (asterism),
having seen it, becomes immediately pure.
Those who have fallen from water, fire, or hanging,
those who have lapsed from renunciation or from a vow of fasting,
those whose bodies have been afflicted by poison,
these nine who have undergone such calamities,
Those sinners who have undergone both kinds of calamity,
who have fallen from the black and spotted cows,
having given a cow and a bull.
One slain by a cow or a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, one who is burnt,
or one who has died by hanging,
having cut the noose of that person,
That which is infested with worms and associated with the sacred,
and that which is contaminated by flies,
and should give a fee according to one's ability.
Having drunk water that has touched a <s>caṇḍāla's</s> vessel,
water that has fallen on the ground,
subsisting on cow's urine and barley gruel,
one becomes purified in six nights.
stored in a <s>caṇḍāla's</s> pot or vessel,
if he vomits it out at that very moment,
If he does not vomit out the water,
and it is digested in his body,
a <s>vaiśya</s> should perform half of that,
and for a <s>śūdra</s>, one-quarter should be imposed.
and likewise having drunk their water,
a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should perform <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance) for a month,
and a fast of one night—
this is known as the <s>sāṃtapana kṛcchra</s> (heated penance).
Those who have the form of <s>caṇḍālas</s>,
having given to them or eaten with them,
A twice-born man who has sexual intercourse
having performed <s>aghamarṣaṇa</s> (sin-removing rite) for a fortnight,
is purified by subsisting on milk.
Thus ends the first chapter of the sacred <s>Yāmya Dharmaśāstra</s>.
a washerwoman, and a woman who lives by bamboo-work,
having gone to them, one should perform <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance),
and likewise a woman who lives by leather-work.
For those who eat the food of <s>kāpālikas</s> (skull-bearers),
and likewise those who approach their own daughters,
if done unknowingly, a <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance) is prescribed,
and if done knowingly, a double observance.
and is purified by the <s>mauñjī homa</s> (sacred grass oblation).
and also a <s>śūdra</s> born in natural order,
one should observe the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance) vow.
One should determine the morsel to be
the size of a hen's egg,
and in case of inability otherwise,
one becomes purified on the ninth day.
One should increase each morsel by one
during the bright half and decrease during the dark half,
and on the new moon day one should not eat—
this is the rule of <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance).
he is purified, and attains the fruit thereof,
in this world and in the next.
As long as one who should be kept separate
they are inauspicious and should not be touched—
They are unfit to eat with, unfit to receive gifts from,
unfit to sit in the same row with, and unfit for marriage alliance,
but when the vow is fulfilled, they are purified,
and all of them become sharers of inheritance.
Thus ends the second chapter of the sacred <s>Yāmya Dharmaśāstra</s>.
For one under eleven years of age,
the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) should be performed by the brother,
or the father, or another relative.
there is no offense and no sin,
there is no royal punishment for him,
Those over eighty years of age,
as do women and the diseased.
Having approached the wife of a paternal uncle or brother,
a sister, or the mother herself,
a mother-in-law, or a paternal aunt,
A queen, or a teacher's female student,
or the wives of a preceptor,
having approached these women through delusion,
one should perform <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance) for six months.
Two months eating only food fit to eat,
thus one should perform the six-month <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance).
Having approached one's own mother, a <s>guru's</s> wife,
and a <s>caṇḍāla</s> or a menstruating woman,
and water brought during the daytime,
by bathing with it and drinking it,
and by touching a cow, one is purified.
these <s>śūdras</s> are those whose food may be eaten,
and also one who offers himself in service.
those ignorant twice-born who eat it,
having thus incurred the need for expiation,
A twice-born who for even one night
engages in the company of a <s>vṛṣalī</s> (low-caste woman),
for eating her food, he should constantly recite prayers—
in three years he removes the sin.
for him there is perpetual impurity,
equivalent to <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>) every day.
in this very birth he becomes a <s>śūdra</s>,
and in the next he will become a dog.
One who has drunk the foam from a <s>vṛṣalī's</s> lips,
and one upon whom her breath has fallen,
and one who has begotten offspring in her—
for him no atonement is prescribed.
Seeing a <s>māhiṣaka</s> (buffalo-keeper) at the beginning of a meal,
a husband of a <s>vṛṣalī</s> in the middle,
and seeing a usurer at the end,
and she is also an adulteress,
he is indeed known as a <s>māhiṣaka</s>.
A girl who, in her father's house,
sees her menses without having been given in marriage,
the sin of embryo-killing falls upon her father,
and that girl is considered a <s>vṛṣalī</s> (outcast woman).
he is not to be spoken to and unfit for communal dining—
that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is a husband of a <s>vṛṣalī</s>.
When the twelfth year has arrived,
he who does not give his daughter in marriage,
month after month the menstrual blood
of that girl is drunk by the father.
At eight years she is called <s>Gaurī</s>,
he who gives for a greater price,
he should be known as a usurer,
condemned among those who expound the <s>Vedas</s>.
A barren woman who causes the destruction of semen
is declared to be one who should be abandoned,
and he who would be her husband—
him one should know as a goat-and-sheep keeper.
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has come to one's house
weary from afar and stricken with fear,
he who eats without honoring him—
at that moment this is ordained for him:
having been touched even by the tip of a blade of grass by them,
one should enter water with one's clothes on.
As long as the food remains hot,
as long as they eat in silence,
the ancestors eat for that duration,
as long as the qualities of the oblation are not spoken.
The qualities of the oblation should not be spoken—
the oblation should be praised as excellent.
As many morsels as one swallows
without being invited at offerings to gods and ancestors,
one swallows in the next life.
One should give a seat upon seats,
when seats are given in the hand,
One who places a foot on the seat,
or whose garment hangs half below,
or who eats food blown upon by mouth—
such a twice-born should perform <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance).
One who, with purificatory rings on the fingers,
if he does not attend to the ancestors,
One who eats while laughing, or with sound,
or by licking, or by rolling the food—
these six are polluters of the dining row.
One with leucoderma, one with leprosy, one with a spear-like affliction,
one with bad nails, and one with discolored teeth,
one who is diseased, one with deficient or extra limbs,
a slanderer, and one who is envious,
a heretic, and one who reviles the <s>Vedas</s>,
a sophist, one who sacrifices for <s>śūdras</s>,
and one who sacrifices for the unworthy,
one who is always greedy for receiving gifts,
a beggar, one addicted to sensual pleasures,
one with discolored teeth, and a physician,
these are to be carefully avoided
a hired servant, and a seller of the <s>Vedas</s>,
these are to be carefully avoided—
the ancestors of such a person become hopeless
and become sharers of his debts.
should be employed in offerings to gods and ancestors—
even with bodily defects that would pollute a row,
<s>Yama</s> declared that he should be excluded,
yet he is indeed a purifier of the dining row.
Free from envy, of good conduct,
learned in the <s>Vedas</s>, and versed in sacred knowledge,
a worthy vessel, the best of twice-born,
one who knows the <s>Vedānta</s>, skilled in the foremost <s>Sāman</s> chants,
free from greed, devoted to the <s>Vedas</s>,
in rites for gods and ancestors,

children.translated_text: for what is eaten and offered to him—
its merit is infinite, there is no doubt.
A twice-born who is touched by one who has leftover food in his mouth,
or by a dog or a <s>śūdra</s>,
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who, having left food in his vessel,
if he touches it through negligence,
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who is touched while having leftover food
by another <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who also has leftover food,
should afterwards recite the <s>Daśarudrī</s> (ten hymns to <s>Rudra</s>)—
When one having leftover food touches another with leftover food—
or when a twice-born is touched through negligence
If a dog, a rooster, a cat,
that twice-born who has leftover food—
he is purified in one day and night,
One who touches a menstruating woman—
for him a penance of three nights should be imposed,
having fasted, with the purificatory rite of a twice-born,
By the glance of a menstruating woman,
bathing, worship of gods, charitable giving,
and fire offerings are all destroyed.
those who live by bamboo-work, fishermen,
carpenters, and those who live by leather-work,
from the touch of these, sin accrues,
and likewise when one is deluded thereby,
and from accepting gifts from them, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>
having fasted for six nights and bathed,
what is the rite for the servant class?
equal to that of their master, it is said.
That which he does not cause to be done—
<s>Yama</s> did not speak of anything else regarding that,
but in marriages, festivals, and sacrifices,
when the occasion has thus arisen,
when a woman sees her menses—
what is the rite for that time?
sprinkled with the hymn 'āpo hiṣṭhā' and other <s>ṛcs</s> (Vedic verses),
after the worship, one should offer oblations
of one hundred and eight ghee offerings,
and then one should proceed with the ceremony.
As long as the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> are not honored
even for one whose vow has been completed,
When the body is touched by crow, crane, or kite droppings,
or smeared with impure fuel at any time,
whether on the ear, mouth, or on the top of the head,
is the purification for one whose body is stained.
Regarding the eating of things that should not be eaten,
should not be drunk, and should not be licked,
and of semen, urine, and feces—
having drunk water infused with these,
If the touch of menstruating women
When menstruating women touch one another,
whether of the same <s>gotra</s> (clan) or a different <s>gotra</s>,
purification is prescribed after three nights.
When menstruating women touch one another—
the former should perform half a <s>kṛcchra</s>,
When menstruating women touch one another—
the former should perform a <s>kṛcchra</s> minus a quarter,
and the latter a single quarter.
When menstruating women touch one another—
the <s>śūdra</s> woman is purified by a full <s>kṛcchra</s>,
and the <s>brāhmaṇī</s> is purified by a gift.
When a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is touched at night
by a menstruating woman or an outcaste,
he should be bathed near a fire
with water brought during the daytime.
During the day, water that has been touched by the sun,
at night, water from which stars are visible,
Thus ends the third chapter of the sacred <s>Yāmya Dharmaśāstra</s>.
An excavation, a reservoir, or a well,
or one struck on stone by a weapon,
or one struck by a stick—
one should remedy it with lumps of earth.
The sin that arises from the killing of a cow,
whether committed by a woman or a man?
A cow that has fallen into a pit,
or into a well or a hollow,
A cow that has fallen by a staff-blow,
or even a bullock that has died,
or a calf or a young bull —
Whether a woman or a boy,
The sinner should publicly confess the sin,
and give a milch-cow and a bull.
they are tormented in the hells
until the dissolution of all beings.
By whom through negligence has been killed
a tawny cow or any other —
As in the sin of slaying a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>,
so too is the sin in slaying a tawny cow.
the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (atonement) is declared to be equal.
by a clod of earth, by fresh cow-dung,
even by the most severe means, the cow-slayer
A cow that has been struck by a fist,
or in a river of dogs, or beyond it —
All this has been told to you,
the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (atonement) is separate in each case.
A cow that has fallen in the forest,
when that cow has indeed died,
Or even a man who was sent [to tend the cow],
for a <s>śūdra</s> it is one year,
for a <s>vaiśya</s> it shall be double.
and for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> it is fourfold.
One should dwell in a cow-pen,
and the cow-slayer should declare: 'I am [a cow-slayer].'
becomes pure by the passage of time.
One should dwell among cows at night,
and during the day one should follow the cows
For women, no tonsure should be performed,
nor is the cow-following observance prescribed.
Nor should she dwell in a cow-pen at night,
nor should she recite Vedic scripture.
what rule is prescribed for that?
Tell us as it truly is.
is absorbed — there is no doubt.
the <s>sūtaka</s> (birth impurity) as prescribed by me shall continue.
One is not tainted by the <s>sūtaka</s> (birth impurity) —
One is not tainted by the <s>sūtaka</s> (birth impurity);
and worship of the gods likewise [are unaffected].
The slayer of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the drinker of liquor,
the stealer of gold, the betrayer of the teacher —
the associate [of these] is known as the fifth,
equal to them — there is no doubt in this.
And for those guilty of <s>pātaka</s> (major sins),
three to five years is ordained.
Eating once a day, then eating at night only,
as the destroyer of sin, it is declared.
<s>prāyaścitta</s> (atonement) should be given by the wise
of living beings who have committed evil.
such indeed is the case for sinners.
but that sin goes to the assembly [that prescribed it].
Therefore, in accordance with the scriptures,
Those who die in the lying-in chamber,
and those who die during a woman's <s>sūtaka</s> (birth impurity),
for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has died in the lying-in chamber,
the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (atonement) is to be performed by the relatives.
It should be done for one year,
and likewise should be given for women.
For the sake of purification, not otherwise —
Those who have met with an untimely death,
and those who have gone to a lower state —
two or three years is especially recommended.
<s>śūdras</s>, and those of the lowest castes,
it should be given in graded measure —
how is purification to be achieved for them,
For women, purification from adultery occurs at the menstrual period —
When a pregnancy has occurred, abandonment [is the rule];
By the very sight of an unchaste woman,
the ancestors go to a lower state.
One should pour ghee into the womb — dreadful [is the sin of]
a woman who has gone to another man.
And oblation should be made with effort,
one hundred and eight in number.
And a widow who is a woman
she should be abandoned by her relatives —
the pronouncement of <s>Yama</s> is not otherwise.
and who has turned away from sin,
It should be given in graded measure —
or even a <s>śūdra</s>, in due order.
The sin of approaching a widow,
and when committed repeatedly and knowingly,
For a single act, the sin [is expiated]
A remarried woman who has been made impure
without the distinction of Vedic branch,
And one of the same <s>varṇa</s> (caste) with a woman of the same <s>varṇa</s>,
when he has been consecrated [in marriage],
is censured at <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites) and sacrifice.
or to a <s>kṣatriya</s> woman, or a <s>vaiśya</s> indeed,
becomes as one who has approached a fallen woman.
In <s>pratiloma</s> (against the natural order) unions, great sin
is not applicable, and not otherwise.
<s>prāyaścitta</s> (atonement) should be performed day by day.
The morning <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight worship) while stars are [still visible],
is indeed for purification from sin.
and likewise one who neglects bathing —
one who neglects bathing is an eater of filth;
one who neglects <s>sandhyā</s> is a slayer of an embryo.
sin [of the night] is destroyed by meditating upon her,
he who is devoted to worship.
He goes to <s>Brahmaloka</s> (the world of Brahmā) —
the pronouncement of <s>Yama</s> is not otherwise.
One who is endowed with knowledge and water [rituals],
peaceful, pure, and free from greed,
such are the gods on earth, without doubt.
They should be known as worthy recipients —
What is given to them yields infinite [merit] —
But those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who engage in evil deeds,
slanderous and attached to sense objects —
what is given to them is fruitless;
there should be no hesitation in this matter.
[Verse corrupt] Regarding acceptance of gifts, one who is restrained... held by others...
[Verse corrupt] ...purifier of sin from seeing the earth... in Kṛta, Tretā, Dvāpara, and Kali ages...
From accepting gifts from a king,
is destroyed — there is no doubt.
Acceptance of gifts from kings should be avoided
by those who aspire to the three worlds.
By accepting gifts from a king,
the status of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is indeed destroyed.
Cows perish by being driven far afield,
a woman is ruined by preg-
and a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> by service to a king.
kings under the guise of meritorious titles,
they are tormented in the <s>Kumbhīpāka</s> (hell of boiling pots)
until the dissolution of all beings.
and who perform sacrifices for the unworthy,
they should be known as excluded from the assembly,
Thus ends the fourth chapter in the venerable <s>Yāmya Dharmaśāstra</s>.
and of the <s>varṇas</s> (castes) and others, in due order.
All matters of contact with women
that arise from those designated as outcastes,
all that is born of the mixture of classes,
in the order of their respective castes —
therefore, the state of being a <s>brāhma</s>-
is declared to be especially authoritative.
and those women who have been forcibly enslaved
such as the killing of cows and other living beings —
in graded measure by the twice-born.
When at the time of <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites),
or has given birth — then neither the divine
nor the ancestral rites should be performed.
having designated the cooking for the ancestors,
the ancestral rite itself should be performed.
Impurity does not apply in this case;
there should be no deliberation on this matter.
If while on a journey, his father
and the <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite) and other [ceremonies] by the son
at the time of giving a daughter [in marriage],
[he] heard that the father had died,
the giving of the daughter should still be completed
The rites for the father, such as the vessel [offerings] and the rest,
should be performed afterwards, all according to proper procedure.

children.text: vyāsenoktasmṛtau svakīye ajñānāt pitari mṛte yadā jñātu sadaiva kāryaṃ pitṛkam eva vā //
children.translated_text: [Prose gloss] As stated in <s>Vyāsa's</s> own <s>smṛti</s>: when the father has died and [the son] learns of it later, the ancestral rite should always be performed.
all that is performed by the eldest
becomes fruitful as an ancestral rite.
For one without a son, the sons [of others] may serve
as performers of the funeral rites.
Neither an adopted [son] nor a deficient one,
one taken by force, one bound [by obligation],
a brother's son, a friend's son,
a pupil, and the natural-born son —
for one without a son, these should be known
as heirs — there is no doubt.
These nine should be maintained as sons;
they are indeed the givers of the next world.
They should be known as equal to the natural-born son —
Now, the determination of shares [in inheritance] —
Whether by the eldest or the youngest,
to those without sons — there is no doubt.
always with the counsel of the sons.
In a pledge, in an acceptance, in a transfer,
the earlier [transaction] is the more valid.
the later evidence is more powerful.
First is the rule of deposit,
and the later [evidence] is of four kinds.
When witnesses exist on both sides,
When the plaintiff's case is weakened,
an ordeal should be administered according to proper procedure.
Thus ends the fifth chapter in the venerable <s>Yāmya Dharmaśāstra</s>.
